refresher.title: Keep unmatched rows with LEFT JOIN
refresher.text: A JOIN matches keys between tables. A LEFT JOIN keeps every row on the left and puts NULL in the right columns when there is no match. Aliases such as r and z name the two table copies. Joining twice lets you look up two locations.

WITH rides(id, place) AS (VALUES (1, 10), (2, 99)),
places(id, name) AS (VALUES (10, 'Depot'))

LEFT JOIN places z ON z.id = r.place;

refresher.title: Label the first matching condition
refresher.text: CASE tests WHEN conditions in order: the first true branch wins. Here 1 meets both conditions but gets first; 2 gets second, and 3 reaches ELSE. In an answer without ELSE, rows that match no branch get NULL. Test missing values with IS NULL.

WITH examples(n) AS (VALUES (1), (2), (3))
SELECT n, CASE WHEN n < 2 THEN 'first'
WHEN n < 3 THEN 'second' ELSE 'other' END AS label
FROM examples;

rulesText:
## Floor 2: Nowhere zones (joins, NULLs and sentinels)

- **Tables given:** `trips` (floor 1's reference output, 7,171 rows), `zones`.
- **The dirt:** real: 110 trips touch zone 264 "Unknown", 74 touch zone 265 "Outside of NYC".
  Planted: 15 drop-off ids are 0 (not in the lookup) and 10 drop-off ids are NULL.
- **Task:** return an answer: every row of `trips`, plus `pu_zone`, `do_zone` (the zone name,
  NULL when there is no match) and `zone_flag`, the first that applies:
  1. `'unmatched'`: either id is NULL or not in `zones`;
  2. `'unknown'`: either id is 264;
  3. `'outside_nyc'`: either id is 265;
  4. `'ok'`.
- **Expected:** 7,171 rows in and out. Flags: ok 6,962; unknown 110; outside_nyc 74; unmatched 25.
  An inner join to `zones` on both ids keeps only 7,146 rows (it silently loses 25).
- **Pass:** 7,171 rows; the multiset of `row_id`, `pu_zone`, `do_zone`, `zone_flag` equals the reference
  data/reference/floor2.sql; all columns of `trips` present and unchanged.
- **Aha line:** a join can drop rows without an error. "Unknown" (264) is in the lookup, so an anti-join cannot find it; a missing id (0, NULL) is not, so only a left join shows it. Flag, do not delete.

solutions.name: valid (a): the reference
solutions.sql:
WITH enriched AS (
SELECT t.*, pz.zone AS pu_zone, dz.zone AS do_zone,
       CASE WHEN pz.location_id IS NULL OR dz.location_id IS NULL THEN 'unmatched'
            WHEN t.pu_location_id = 264 OR t.do_location_id = 264 THEN 'unknown'
            WHEN t.pu_location_id = 265 OR t.do_location_id = 265 THEN 'outside_nyc'
            ELSE 'ok' END AS zone_flag
FROM trips t
LEFT JOIN zones pz ON pz.location_id = t.pu_location_id
LEFT JOIN zones dz ON dz.location_id = t.do_location_id
) SELECT * FROM enriched;

solutions.name: valid (b): correlated subqueries for the names, CASE tests a NULL name first
solutions.sql:
SELECT *, CASE WHEN pu_zone IS NULL OR do_zone IS NULL THEN 'unmatched'
                           WHEN pu_location_id = 264 OR do_location_id = 264 THEN 'unknown'
                           WHEN pu_location_id = 265 OR do_location_id = 265 THEN 'outside_nyc'
                           ELSE 'ok' END AS zone_flag
            FROM (SELECT t.*, (SELECT z.zone FROM zones z WHERE z.location_id = t.pu_location_id) AS pu_zone,
                              (SELECT z.zone FROM zones z WHERE z.location_id = t.do_location_id) AS do_zone
                  FROM trips t)

Floor 2: Nowhere zones

Cleared

Trips to nowhere

{{context}} {{refresher}}

Some trips start or end in a zone that is not a real place on the map. If you join to the zone lookup the wrong way, those trips vanish without an error.

{{task}}

Lv 2 · How the check works

The check compares values, not formatting: 1.10 and 1.1 are the same, and money is compared to the cent.

You get trips (rerun copies already removed, 7,171 rows) and zones (265 rows). pu_zone and do_zone are the zone names from zones, or NULL when there is no match.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

SELECT * FROM zones WHERE location_id IN (264, 265);

Three kinds of nowhere

  • Zone 264 is "Unknown". The lookup has it, but it names no place.
  • Zone 265 is "Outside of NYC". It is a real place, outside the zone map.
  • Some drop-off ids are 0 or NULL. They match nothing in the lookup.

Lv 2 · How the check works

110 trips touch zone 264, and 74 touch zone 265. These are real TLC rows. 25 trips have a drop-off id that matches nothing: 15 are 0 and 10 are NULL. These are planted for the game.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

SELECT do_location_id, count(*) AS trips
FROM trips
WHERE do_location_id IS NULL
   OR do_location_id NOT IN (SELECT location_id FROM zones)
GROUP BY do_location_id;

A join can drop rows

An inner join keeps only rows that match on both sides. The trips with no matching drop-off zone disappear, and nothing warns you.

Lv 2 · How the check works

With an inner join on both ids, 7,171 trips become 7,146. A LEFT JOIN keeps every trip and puts NULL where there is no match.

An anti-join (a LEFT JOIN where the lookup side IS NULL) lists the rows that match nothing. It cannot find zone 264, because 264 is in the lookup.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

SELECT count(*) FROM trips t
JOIN zones pz ON pz.location_id = t.pu_location_id
JOIN zones dz ON dz.location_id = t.do_location_id;  -- 7,146

SELECT t.row_id, t.do_location_id
FROM trips t
LEFT JOIN zones dz ON dz.location_id = t.do_location_id
WHERE dz.location_id IS NULL;  -- the 25 that match nothing

Flag, do not delete

Keep every row, and add a flag that says what is wrong. Someone later can choose what to do with it. A deleted row cannot be explained later.

Lv 2 · How the check works

zone_flag takes the first rule that applies, in this order:

  1. 'unmatched': either id is NULL or not in zones;
  2. 'unknown': either id is 264;
  3. 'outside_nyc': either id is 265;
  4. 'ok'.

The order matters: test 'unmatched' first.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

CASE WHEN ___ /* a pickup or drop-off with no match */ THEN 'unmatched'
     WHEN pu_location_id = 264 OR do_location_id = 264 THEN 'unknown'
     WHEN ___ /* ... 265 ... */ THEN 'outside_nyc'
     ELSE 'ok' END AS zone_flag

Count before and after

7,171 rows in, 7,171 rows out. No row is lost, and each one carries a flag.

Lv 2 · How the check works

Flags: ok 6,962, unknown 110, outside_nyc 74, unmatched 25. Together they make 7,171.

The check passes when your answer has 7,171 rows, keeps every column of trips unchanged, and has the expected row_id, pu_zone, do_zone, zone_flag values.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

WITH answer AS (___ /* your answer query */)
SELECT zone_flag, count(*) AS trips
FROM answer
GROUP BY zone_flag
ORDER BY trips DESC;

trips_raw

zones

Lv 3 · The real SQL

SELECT * FROM zones WHERE location_id IN (264, 265);

Three kinds of nowhere

  • Zone 264 is "Unknown". The lookup has it, but it names no place.
  • Zone 265 is "Outside of NYC". It is a real place, outside the zone map.
  • Some drop-off ids are 0 or NULL. They match nothing in the lookup.

Lv 2 · How the check works

110 trips touch zone 264, and 74 touch zone 265. These are real TLC rows. 25 trips have a drop-off id that matches nothing: 15 are 0 and 10 are NULL. These are planted for the game.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

SELECT do_location_id, count(*) AS trips
FROM trips
WHERE do_location_id IS NULL
   OR do_location_id NOT IN (SELECT location_id FROM zones)
GROUP BY do_location_id;

A join can drop rows

An inner join keeps only rows that match on both sides. The trips with no matching drop-off zone disappear, and nothing warns you.

Lv 2 · How the check works

With an inner join on both ids, 7,171 trips become 7,146. A LEFT JOIN keeps every trip and puts NULL where there is no match.

An anti-join (a LEFT JOIN where the lookup side IS NULL) lists the rows that match nothing. It cannot find zone 264, because 264 is in the lookup.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

SELECT count(*) FROM trips t
JOIN zones pz ON pz.location_id = t.pu_location_id
JOIN zones dz ON dz.location_id = t.do_location_id;  -- 7,146

SELECT t.row_id, t.do_location_id
FROM trips t
LEFT JOIN zones dz ON dz.location_id = t.do_location_id
WHERE dz.location_id IS NULL;  -- the 25 that match nothing

Flag, do not delete

Keep every row, and add a flag that says what is wrong. Someone later can choose what to do with it. A deleted row cannot be explained later.

Lv 2 · How the check works

zone_flag takes the first rule that applies, in this order:

  1. 'unmatched': either id is NULL or not in zones;
  2. 'unknown': either id is 264;
  3. 'outside_nyc': either id is 265;
  4. 'ok'.

The order matters: test 'unmatched' first.

Lv 3 · The real SQL

CASE WHEN ___ /* a pickup or drop-off with no match */ THEN 'unmatched'
     WHEN pu_location_id = 264 OR do_location_id = 264 THEN 'unknown'
     WHEN ___ /* ... 265 ... */ THEN 'outside_nyc'
     ELSE 'ok' END AS zone_flag

WITH enriched AS (
SELECT t.*, pz.zone AS pu_zone, dz.zone AS do_zone,
       CASE WHEN pz.location_id IS NULL OR dz.location_id IS NULL THEN 'unmatched'
            WHEN t.pu_location_id = 264 OR t.do_location_id = 264 THEN 'unknown'
            WHEN t.pu_location_id = 265 OR t.do_location_id = 265 THEN 'outside_nyc'
            ELSE 'ok' END AS zone_flag
FROM trips t
LEFT JOIN zones pz ON pz.location_id = t.pu_location_id
LEFT JOIN zones dz ON dz.location_id = t.do_location_id
) SELECT * FROM enriched;
